beats.text: Five thousand Americans guessed how much the richest fifth owns. They were way off.
Then they built the split they would wish for.
Five people, from richest to poorest. Each coin is one percent of all wealth.
Their guess: the richest fifth has fifty-nine coins.
The truth: eighty-four. The poorest two fifths share less than one coin.

sources: Norton & Ariely (2011), Building a Better America – One Wealth Quintile at a Time, Perspectives on Psychological Science 6(1), 9–12 – N = 5,522 Americans (online panel); estimated share of the top quintile ≈ 59 %, ideal ≈ 32 %, actual 84 % (actual quintiles 84 / 11 / 4 / 0.2 / 0.1 %, Wolff data for 2004). Only the top-fifth values are exact in the video; the other estimated and ideal bars are schematic. Critique: some respondents may have thought of income rather than wealth.
